title: Democrat Amy Acton Flips Ohio Governor's Seat, Ending 20-Year GOP Streak
snippet: Dr. Amy Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in a high-stakes Ohio gubernatorial race, handing Democrats a major victory in a state Donald Trump won easily in 2024.
content:
COLUMBUS, Ohio — Former state health director Dr. Amy Acton has won the Ohio governor's race, delivering a seismic victory for Democrats and ending a two-decade Republican stronghold on the state's executive mansion. The Associated Press called the race Tuesday evening, reporting that Acton secured 50.8% of the vote against Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy's 45.9%, with 86% of ballots counted.

The open-seat contest, triggered by outgoing Republican Gov. Mike DeWine reaching his term limits, marked a dramatic political turn for the Buckeye State. Trump backed Ramaswamy heavily in a state he had carried by double digits in the 2024 presidential election, making Acton's victory a major upset and a striking setback for the GOP.

A Bitter Final Stretch Driven by Backlash

The dynamics of the race shifted dramatically in October following a highly contentious attack ad released by Ramaswamy's campaign. The advertisement featured Acton's estranged biological mother, re-examining childhood trauma surrounding the 1978 indictment of Acton's stepfather for sexual abuse when Acton was 12 years old. The ad drew immediate and widespread condemnation across the political spectrum.

Acton's brother, Philip Stearns, publicly denounced the ad as a 'despicable low,' condemning the attempt to turn childhood abuse into a political talking point. Even incumbent Republican Gov. DeWine called the ad 'deeply, deeply troubling' and urged the campaign to pull it, though he maintained his support for the broader Republican ticket. Ramaswamy refused to back down, drawing public defense from both Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance.

The backlash heavily impacted the electorate. Nonpartisan forecasters at The Cook Political Report adjusted their ratings in late October, shifting the race from 'Lean Republican' to 'Toss Up,' and eventually to 'Lean Democrat' in the final days of the campaign.

Acton, who gained statewide prominence for her leadership during the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic, capitalized on the momentum to pull off a historical win, marking the first time an Ohio governorship has flipped to Democrats in 20 years.
